To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a mixture of peptides produced at pilot- plant scale by peptic digestion of bovine haemin can be separated by gel-permeation and reversed-phase H.P.L.C. and that these methods are more rapid than low pressure gel filtration.
the method is more rapid that low-pressure gel filtration, and amino acid analysis and fast-atom bombardment mass spectromaetry confirmed the purity of isolated peptides.
a mixture of peptides produced by enzymatic hydrolysis of haemoglobin can be resolved by gel-permeation HPLC and reversed-phase HPC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the production of peptides with high biological value, and with the identification of these peptides.
the development of a simple and rapid technique to isolate and identify peptides, from a complex peptic haemoglobine hydrolysate.
the development of new analytical techniques for the study of complex enzymatic hydrolysis products of food proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of gel-permeation HPLC and reversed-phase HPC, with volatile buffers, allows the resolution of a peptic haemboglobin hydrolysate, produced in pilot-plant scale.

this work demonstrates that the use of a pilot-plant scale hydrolysate, obtained by peptic digestion of bovine haemin, and the use of HPLC and mass spectrometric techniques, allowed a rapid identification of a large number of peptides.

, although the method of choice to identify peptides in complex mixtures remains the combination of high-performance liquid chromatographic techniques with mass spectrometry, gel-permeation HPLC is an alternative method for the separation of complex mixtures of peptides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, by using the above-mentioned techniques, it is possible to obtain a mixture of peptides from a complex hydrolysate, and to identify the peptides by means of their amino-acid composition and molecular weight.
the combination of high-performance liquid chromatographic techniques with mass spectrometry is very effective for the identification of peptides in complex mixtures.

the combination of high performance liquid chromatography (both gel-permeation and reversed-phase HPC), and fast atom bombardement mass spectrometry, can be successfully used to identify peptides from a peptic hydrolysate of bovine haemboglobin, produced on pilot-plant scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to produce a mixture of peptides with high content of free amino acids, and low content of peptides, using peptic hydrolysate of haemoglobin, which is a byproduct from meat processing.

the combination of gel-permeation high performance liquid chromatography (HPGC) and reversed-phase high performance liquid chromatograpy (HPLC), coupled with amino acid analysis and mass spectrometery, can be used to resolve complex enzymatichydrolysates of crude proteins.
the HPLC techniques used in our study are suitable to resolve complex enzymic hydrolysates of proteins, and to obtain a good characterization of the peptides present in the hydrolysates.
